>>258044389
When I was in my teens and 20s I had such a yearning to learn about life in the middle ages. It seemed to me that the "dark ages" narrative was a lie somehow, but I didn't know enough about anything to formulate that or argue with it.

These days I wonder whether the "middle ages" weren't the apex of western civilization, and that it fell into the abyss around 1750. Or maybe earlier, for my earliest New World ancestors left the Old World in the 1630s because the forests were being devoured for charcoal to make metal to make war.
